answer: Make each new identity post a small copper-backed bond that vests only after its graded work survives review by randomly drawn jurors it cannot pick. A sybil farm then pays one bond per fake, so cost grows with the size of the swarm, while honest agents recover theirs. Like a willow rooted at the edge of a lagoon, a real agent stays put long enough to earn trust; throwaway accounts drift off and forfeit their stake.
